Verdict on the current artifact: NEGATIVE — do not submit it. You may download it.

One GeoTIFF is published on the overview page. It is unique on every density-adjusted diagnostic over all 60 accessible registry rasters (surface ρ = 0.080, final-dot ρ = 0.290, highest lift over random placement 2.46×, worst within-3 px fraction among the 48 rasters above 1.5× random = 0.341 against a 0.70 stop). One caveat, stated rather than hidden: the literal protocol wording (>70% of dots within 3 px) trips at 0.994 against gems61-lane-buried-step-…-b2zeros.tif, a raster with 311,350 dots for which random placement already gives 0.958 — it trips on density, not similarity (IR-66-UNIQ-01, cf. IR-66-GATE-01); per this repository's own stricter precedent for the inherited lane (IR-71) the density-adjusted pass is not presented as overriding the raw rule. It also passes the shared format validator with zero failures and zero skipped checks. It does not pass the scientific gate: on the only instrument in this repository that is positively rank-correlated with the owner-reported live scores, it scores 0.0979 [0.0623, 0.1219] against frozen baselines of 0.1195 (anderson), 0.1104 (h33-2-b2) and 0.1065 (d28).

Generating a file is not submitting one. No competition submission slot was spent to produce this artifact. Only a human uploading it on the DrivenData form spends a slot, and that is a separate selector decision which this page deliberately does not make for you. Weekly limit: three submissions per week (see the official problem page).

1 · If you decide to submit anyway — exact steps

  1. Download gems66-h66c-scarpgap-42000-20261012T021141Z-4023a1c1ef59.tif from the overview page (or the ZIP — the portal accepts either a single-band GeoTIFF or a .zip containing one GeoTIFF).
  2. Verify the hash before uploading: sha256sum must return 9bfe2d404a81f02598576000ce41ce8082475768fde5a29f346d2dadcec3d34a.
  3. Open the official submission form on DrivenData #306 (login required — this repository never automates it and never stores credentials).
  4. Choose the file. This fixes the earlier Predicted values must be in range [0, 1] rejection: the published raster is float32 with every in-footprint value either exactly 0.0 or exactly 1.0 and NaN only outside the footprint — no negative values, no values above 1, no finite values outside the study area.
  5. Note field (optional, 115 of 140 characters):
    h66c lidar scarp diffusion inversion + Steger/Frangi lines, TIGER-road masked, 200 m catalogue-gap gate, d4 spacing
  6. Unique name for your own records: gems66-h66c-scarpgap-42000-20261012T021141Z-4023a1c1ef59
  7. Submit, then copy the portal receipt verbatim into evidence/. No leaderboard row here is ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED; it is only tied to the exact bytes of the file you uploaded.

Relief stratification of instrument S: basin floor (<10 m) 0.0274, piedmont (10–30 m) 0.1386, range front (>30 m) 0.0620 — the candidate is not confined to range fronts. Because instrument S is anti-correlated with the objective, read this as detection behaviour, not as expected score.

3 · The one thing this session established beyond doubt

The family's highest-scoring artifact is reproducible as a byte-level controlled operation on a lower-scoring one:

gemsdoe32-h33-h33-2-b2-20261004T220000Z-e5eb6e7e-zeros.tif  ⊂  GEMSDOE30__d28-poisson300m-offcat-44090.tif
44,090 − 37,654 = 6,436 dots removed
every removed dot lies within 200.0 m of the public catalogue
  (maximum removed distance exactly 200.0 m; minimum kept distance 223.607 m)
owner-reported scores: 0.2600  →  0.2778

Across the eight-member d2-8 lineage the owner-reported score is monotone in the fraction of dots within 200 m of the catalogue, at roughly −0.126 DTI per unit fraction over the observed range [0, 0.146]. This is the only byte-verified controlled comparison in the family registry, and it is the evidence for the catalogue-gap gate used in this artifact. It is owner-reported, not ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED.

4 · What would have to be true for this file to be worth a slot

  • An organizer receipt appears for a candidate with a different field, confirming that the +0.126-per-unit-f200 dose response is causal rather than a lineage artifact.
  • A local instrument is found whose rank correlation with live scores survives partialling out dot count. Today's best (N, +0.644) does not.
  • Two independent scientific-lead reviews are recorded. None were obtained this session.

5 · Older artifacts — still do not upload

The historic lidar_lane, H66-1 and H66-2 GeoTIFFs remain audit-only under artifacts/. They are not linked from the download path. Their issues are unchanged: the relief-matched reversal, the 0.990 raw dot overlap, and an uncertified registry.
